title: Pentagon Publishes More UFO Files Amid Growing Public Curiosity
excerpt: The Pentagon released more than three dozen new UFO files, including videos and documents from around the world. The files feature mysterious sightings, pilot accounts, and artistic renderings, but officials give no explanations for the phenomena.
content:
The Pentagon has released a new batch of declassified UFO files, adding over three dozen reports, videos, and images to the growing archive of unexplained aerial phenomena. The files, released Friday (November 20), mark the eighth such release since President Donald Trump ordered increased transparency on the subject earlier this year, according to The Independent.

Among the newly public documents is a report detailing a plan for a government contractor to construct an underground facility for storing "exotic material or tissue" that could be obtained from unidentified phenomena. However, there is no record that the facility was ever built.

The Pentagon’s files include over forty documents, such as videos of mysterious orbs and spheres captured by U.S. military sensors in locations around the world. According to BBC News, recent footage shows a "cold orb" moving irregularly over the Gulf of Oman in 2021, and a black sphere traveling above the Pacific Ocean in 2019 before vanishing and reappearing. Some videos, like a 2020 infrared clip from a U.S. warship in the Middle East, display circular lights or objects moving in unexplained ways.

Witness testimony also features in the release. A 1953 report from Lockheed engineer Clarence “Kelly” Johnson describes seeing a dark blue "saucer" in California, accompanied by hand-drawn sketches, as reported by The Independent. In another instance, two senior military officials described witnessing a black triangle-shaped object hovering and then silently descending into a canyon at a sensitive site in the western United States in June 2026, according to USA Today.

Many of the files contain artistic renderings based on eyewitness accounts, with one image depicting a vast black triangle in the sky, its corners marked by round lights. Some of the documents also include accounts from commercial pilots who have seen unusual lights during flights.

Despite the compelling visuals and stories, Pentagon officials maintain that they are "not providing any comment or assessment on the files overall or on any specific file," allowing the public to "make up their own minds regarding the files," according to The Independent. The Department of Defense has emphasized that many sightings have mundane explanations, such as misidentified aircraft or camera artifacts.

Public interest in unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP), the term now used for UFOs, has surged in recent years, fueled by congressional hearings and calls for greater government transparency. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, cited by BBC News, said additional files will be released on a "rolling basis" in the future.
